title: Reduced differentials of an arbitrary tensor product
statement: Let A,R,S,B,Q be commutative rings, let R and B be A-algebras, and let S be an R-algebra with an A-algebra structure compatible with A -> R -> S. Let Q be an A-algebra, and let sigma:B -> Q, eta:R -> Q, tau:S tensor_A B -> Q be A-algebra maps satisfying tau(1 tensor b)=sigma(b) and tau(algebraMap_R(S tensor_A B)(r))=eta(r). Write D=S tensor_A B and theta(s)=tau(s tensor 1). Then Q tensor_D Omega[D/R] is Q-linearly isomorphic to (Q tensor_B Omega[B/A]) times (Q tensor_S Omega[S/R]), where Q is acted on via tau,sigma,theta respectively. The differential modules are as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]; tensor extension is as in [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-universal-property]. No flatness or finiteness is assumed.

proof.text: Set X=(Q tensor_B Omega[B/A]) times (Q tensor_S Omega[S/R]). Obtain derivations dB(b)=(1 tensor db,0) and dS(s)=(0,1 tensor ds) by composing universal derivations with the canonical tensor maps and product inclusions. Each produces an algebra map into the trivial square-zero extension Q plus X, with first component sigma or theta and second component dB or dS. The scalar-tower identities follow from hSigma,hEta and the algebra-homomorphism compatibility with A.

Apply Algebra.TensorProduct.lift to the two algebra maps, obtaining H:D -> Q plus X. Its first component is tau: on s tensor b both are theta(s)sigma(b). Its second component d is an R-derivation, since the square-zero product formula is Leibniz. On s tensor 1 it equals dS(s); on 1 tensor b it equals dB(b). Differential universality and extension of scalars give the Q-linear forward map f:Q tensor_D Omega[D/R] -> X.

Compose the universal derivation of D with Omega[D/R] -> Q tensor_D Omega[D/R]. Restrict it to S, and restrict its A-scalar restriction to B. Lift the resulting derivations through differentials and extension of scalars to gS and gB; their coproduct is g:X -> Q tensor_D Omega[D/R]. For f g=id, test on the two tensor-differential generators and use the restriction formulas for d. For g f=id, g composed with d equals the base-changed universal derivation of D: they agree on s tensor 1 and 1 tensor b, hence on their products s tensor b by Leibniz, hence on all D by tensor induction. Differential and tensor extensionality give the identity on Q tensor_D Omega[D/R]. These two identities construct the equivalence.

lean.statement:
theorem reduced_tensor_differentials
    (A R S B Q : Type u)
    [CommRing A] [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing B] [CommRing Q]
    [Algebra A R] [Algebra R S] [Algebra A S] [IsScalarTower A R S]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A Q]
    (σ : B →ₐ[A] Q) (η : R →ₐ[A] Q) (τ : (S ⊗[A] B) →ₐ[A] Q)
    (hσ : τ.comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight = σ)
    (hη : ∀ r : R, τ (algebraMap R (S ⊗[A] B) r) = η r) :
    letI : Algebra B Q := σ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra R Q := η.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra S Q := (τ.comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft).toRingHom.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra (S ⊗[A] B) Q := τ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    Nonempty ((Q ⊗[S ⊗[A] B] KaehlerDifferential R (S ⊗[A] B)) ≃ₗ[Q]
      ((Q ⊗[B] KaehlerDifferential A B) × (Q ⊗[S] KaehlerDifferential R S)))
